EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2877 and 2963 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003) and a pronounced CH₂ deformation near 1463 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003), consistent with a saturated hydrocarbon framework. The very intense, narrow band at 821 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a cyclohexane-type ring breathing mode, and accompanying ring-related bands appear near 943–961, 1053, and 1126 cm⁻¹. Linear alcohols would typically exhibit a strong methylene rocking around ~720 cm⁻¹, which is absent here, while acetal/ether rings (e.g., dioxolanes) tend to have ring-breathing/C–O–C modes at higher (~860–950) wavenumbers. These features best match a substituted cyclohexanol, supporting candidate 4.
